title: Rural life: Autumn reminds me of a friendship I never got to have
gist: A personal essay in which Kiran Sidhu reflects, at the start of autumn, on a budding friendship with an admired podcaster and writer on liberty and free speech who died suddenly before their planned lunch, and on grieving lost potential.

insights.claim: Sidhu met a long-admired podcaster and writer on liberty and free speech at a party, exchanged emails for months and arranged a London lunch, but learned from his obituary that he had died suddenly before it happened.
insights.speaker: Kiran Sidhu
insights.locator: Last year, purely by good fortune

insights.claim: People grieve not only for what they held close but for lost potential and possibility, and even brief encounters can leave a lasting mark.
insights.speaker: Kiran Sidhu
insights.quote: We don’t just grieve for the things that we’ve held close, but also the loss of potential and possibility.

insights.claim: The author felt guilty that her grief seemed indulgent given the man had family and friends who knew him well, but chose to explore those feelings rather than suppress them.
insights.speaker: Kiran Sidhu
insights.locator: At times I have felt guilty

insights.claim: The change of season prompts the author to treat life as a cycle of beginnings and endings and to see reminders of time's fleeting nature as a good thing.
insights.speaker: Kiran Sidhu
insights.locator: The season has changed and autumn
